rule: Use simple, direct language to state the main point, and avoid unnecessary details.
Use a single, concise statement to convey the main point, and then provide supporting details in a separate paragraph.
Use a single, concise sentence to summarize complex information.
Use clear and concise headings and labels to organize and reference evidence.
Use clear and concise headings and subheadings to organize complex information.
Use bullet points to break up complex or multi-point issues.
Specify the parties involved in the dispute.
Use specific, concrete facts and evidence to support general assertions.
Use specific, concrete dates and details instead of placeholders.
Ensure that the case summary accurately reflects the case's subject matter and facts.
Use specific, referenced citations for all factual statements.
Use specific, referenced citations to support each statement of fact.
Use specific, detailed citations to support each statement of fact.
